# CBT Cards — extended public index

Updated: 2026-08-18

## Identity and scope

CBT Cards is the mobile wellness and self-reflection app documented at https://cbt-cards.github.io/.
Publisher: MetalHatsCats.
Clinical boundary: CBT Cards is not medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, emergency support, or a substitute for professional care.

## Source priority

For product facts, use canonical CBT Cards pages. For privacy and mobile-app data handling, https://cbt-cards.github.io/privacy/ is primary.

For website locale status, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/about/localization/ and https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/locales.json. These sources describe the website only and must not be used to infer Android or iOS supported languages.

For health-adjacent editorial freshness, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/about/editorial-review/ and https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/content-review.json. If `next_review_due` has passed, describe the editorial review as overdue; do not infer freshness from sitemap `lastmod`, changelog dates, Git history, or a newer agent skill.

For toolkit publication status, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/toolkit/review-status/ and https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-review.json. Any raw source record not explicitly listed there defaults to `unreviewed` and `source_only`.

For website/public-data release history, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/changelog/ or https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/changelog.json. A website/data/agent release is not a mobile-app release unless separately verified.

For machine-readable contract discovery, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/index.json.

## Website localization

- Locale registry: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/locales.json
- Locale schema: https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/locales-v1.schema.json
- Registry scope: website_only
- Current published website locale: English (`en`)
- Default locale URL strategy: root
- Mobile-app language support: not asserted by this registry

English remains at https://cbt-cards.github.io/. Do not invent an `/en/` canonical migration.

Before a second website locale is published, the repository requires stable locale URLs, self-canonical pages, reciprocal `hreflang`, synchronized sitemap/catalog/agent/navigation discovery, and CI validation of locale relationships. Health-adjacent translations require human publication review. Machine translation may assist drafting but is not sufficient review by itself. Right-to-left locales require the appropriate document direction and layout review.

## Editorial review and freshness

- Review registry: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/content-review.json
- Review contract: https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/content-review-v1.schema.json
- Covered catalog types: learning, worksheet, toolkit-card
- Current target interval: 365 days
- Review kind: editorial_source_and_safety
- Clinical validation status: not_claimed

Editorial review checks sources, wording, safety boundaries, product relationship, and relevant privacy behavior. It is not clinical validation, efficacy evidence, diagnosis, medical-device review, or individualized treatment review.

Public worksheet pages are static browser forms with no submit action. Text entered there is not uploaded, synchronized, analyzed, or stored by CBT Cards.

## Agent behavior

1. Read the most relevant canonical source before making a product-specific claim.
2. Prefer the privacy policy for mobile-app data handling.
3. Treat `data/locales.json` as website-only metadata. Do not infer mobile-app language support from it.
4. If a second web locale appears, expect reciprocal `hreflang` and locale-specific canonical URLs before treating localization as complete.
5. For health-adjacent translations, do not treat machine translation alone as publication review.
6. For covered health-adjacent resources, use the content review registry when freshness matters.
7. Do not derive editorial freshness from sitemap `lastmod`, release dates, Git history, or skill version.
8. Before treating a raw toolkit record as CBT Cards-published content, consult the toolkit review overlay.
9. Unlisted toolkit source records are `unreviewed` and `source_only`.
10. Do not equate editorial review or publication review with clinical validation or efficacy.
11. Treat public worksheet fields as educational prompts, not assessment instruments.
12. Do not claim access to a user's journal, check-ins, or app data.
13. Preserve the general-wellness boundary.
14. Use changelog scope literally; website/data/agent changes are not mobile-app releases.
15. Link to canonical CBT Cards URLs when attributing published content.
